title: Blueprint node finitary-Carleson: finitary Carleson bound proved from four upstream nodes
intent: Freeze the statement and Lean name of the node `finitary-Carleson` before its proof, then prove the finitary Carleson bound by composing four already-stated upstream nodes, each declared in one `\uses{}` line: a grid and a tile structure carry the continuous operator to a dyadic model, `discrete-Carleson` gives the dyadic bound, and `tile-sum-operator` carries it back to the original operator.

parent.name: finitary-Carleson
parent.statement: If σ1, σ2 : X → ℤ are measurable functions with finite range and σ1 ≤ σ2, and F, G are bounded Borel sets in X, then there is a Borel set G' in X with 2μ(G') ≤ μ(G) such that for all Borel functions f : X → ℂ with |f| ≤ 1_F, ∫_{G \ G'} |Σ_{s=σ1(x)}^{σ2(x)} ∫ K_s(x,y) f(y) e(Ϙ(x)(y)) dμ(y)| dμ(x) ≤ (2^{442a³}/(q-1)⁵) μ(G)^{1-1/q} μ(F)^{1/q} (Lean name finitary_carleson).

children.name: discrete-Carleson
children.statement: For a grid structure (𝒟, c, s) and a tile structure (𝒫, 𝗊, ...) for it, the dyadic model bound: there is a Borel set G' with 2μ(G') ≤ μ(G) such that for all Borel f with |f| ≤ 1_F, ∫_{G \ G'} |Σ_{p∈𝒫} T_p f(x)| dμ(x) ≤ (2^{442a³}/(q-1)⁵) μ(G)^{1-1/q} μ(F)^{1/q}.
children.closed_by: cited via \Cref{discrete-Carleson} at line 1263 to obtain the set G' and the dyadic bound (disclesssim), and again in the final estimate at line 1307; in Lean `rcases discrete_carleson X with ⟨G', hG', h2G', hfG'⟩` (FinitaryCarleson.lean L117)

children.name: grid-existence
children.statement: There exists a grid structure (𝒟, c, s).
children.closed_by: instantiated at line 1261 ('Choose a grid structure ... with \Cref{grid-existence}'); in Lean `have g : GridStructure X D κ S o := grid_existence X` (FinitaryCarleson.lean L114)

children.name: tile-structure
children.statement: For a given grid structure (𝒟, c, s), there exists a tile structure (𝒫, 𝗊, 𝓼, 𝓽, 𝓰, 𝓲).
children.closed_by: instantiated for that grid at line 1262 ('a tile structure ... with \Cref{tile-structure}'); in Lean `have t : TileStructure Q D κ S o := tile_existence X` (FinitaryCarleson.lean L115)

children.name: tile-sum-operator
children.statement: For all x ∈ G \ G', Σ_{p∈𝒫} T_p f(x) = Σ_{s=σ1(x)}^{σ2(x)} ∫ K_s(x,y) f(y) e(Ϙ(x)(y) - Ϙ(x)(x)) dμ(y).
children.closed_by: used at line 1307 ('We now estimate with \Cref{tile-sum-operator} and \Cref{discrete-Carleson}') to rewrite the tile sum as the original operator; in Lean `tile_sum_operator hx` inside the simp_rw at FinitaryCarleson.lean L120

applicability.goal_shape: A lemma or theorem stated as a named node of a dependency graph, with its statement and Lean name frozen before its proof and a single \uses{} line declaring the upstream nodes it depends on; the proof then composes those nodes by citation rather than new construction.
applicability.use_when: the result is a known combination of already-stated (or already-proved) nodes; the statement can be frozen, with its Lean name and \leanok, before the proof; the dependencies can be listed up front (\uses{}) so sufficiency is checkable against a fixed list; the proof may live elsewhere (a later section, or a separate Lean file) and only cite the nodes.
applicability.avoid_when: the proof needs a new construction or a new lemma that must itself be stated and proved (that belongs as its own node in the graph); the statement may still change (then do not fix the Lean name yet); or the cited nodes' hypotheses do not line up into a single composition, in which case forcing them into a linear citation chain leaves gaps.

claims.claim: The parent node is stated with \lean{finitary_carleson}\leanok (line 447) and a \uses{discrete-Carleson, grid-existence, tile-structure, tile-sum-operator} line (line 448) naming four upstream nodes, before its proof (lines 1303-1320).

The proof of the node (lines 1303-1320) closes the bound by citing \Cref{tile-sum-operator} and \Cref{discrete-Carleson} at line 1307 and ends 'This proves ... and thus completes the proof of Proposition finitary-Carleson', introducing no new node.

Each of the four labels in \uses{} is defined at its own site in the same file with a \label{} and a \lean{} name: discrete-Carleson (L552-556), grid-existence (L1239-1243), tile-structure (L1252-1256), tile-sum-operator (L1266-1269), so the dependency cone is a set of named nodes rather than inline proof text.
The node cites 4 upstream nodes (the comma-separated \uses{} list on line 448), with a statement of 15 lines (444-458) and a proof of 18 lines (1303-1320).

consequences: Freezing the statement first means the Lean name finitary_carleson must correspond to a provable Lean statement; if the statement later changes, the name and the \lean{} marker change with it. The four children are discharged in a fixed order — grid-existence and tile-structure produce the grid and tile structures, discrete-Carleson consumes them to give the set G' and the dyadic bound, and tile-sum-operator rewrites the tile sum back to the original operator — so each citation's hypotheses are met only in that state; invoking one earlier leaves a gap. A citation whose hypotheses do not line up leaves a silent gap, because \leanok is a claim the project's build verifies, not something the LaTeX text itself enforces. The proof is split across two places (the LaTeX proof and Carleson/FinitaryCarleson.lean), so the two must be kept in correspondence.
